prompt.brief: Design a durable video media pipeline for resumable uploads, validation, transcoding into adaptive-bitrate renditions, thumbnails, moderation hooks, and CDN delivery.
successSignals: Define upload sessions, immutable source objects, job graphs, codec profiles, rendition manifests, content ownership, and publication state.
Make large uploads resumable and processing idempotent; isolate expensive workers, enforce quotas, and prioritize interactive jobs.
Handle corrupt media, retries, partial outputs, poison jobs, cancellation, moderation/legal holds, retention, and CDN invalidation.
Explain cost/quality tradeoffs, encryption, access control, observability, replay, and degraded delivery.

functional: Create resumable uploads, validate media, enqueue a versioned processing graph, generate renditions/thumbnails, and publish a manifest.
Expose progress, retry/cancel, playback-ready status, signed delivery URLs, adaptive bitrate selection, and content moderation state.
Support replacement/deletion, legal holds, failed-job quarantine, replay from source objects, and cleanup of unreferenced outputs.
nonFunctional: Acknowledge uploads quickly and make 95% of standard jobs playback-ready within the defined processing SLA.
Process 1,000 hours of video daily with burst capacity and bounded asynchronous workers, without a single hot key.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 1,000 hours/day; 10x upload bursts; multi-terabyte source retention
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Durable video media pipeline commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Durable video media pipeline writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Durable video media pipeline version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Durable video media pipeline by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Durable video media pipeline work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Durable video media pipeline projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Durable video media pipeline projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Durable video media pipeline records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Durable video media pipeline latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
